ambiguities.text: The EIP does not specify whether COINBASE warming applies to all transaction types equally (legacy, EIP-2930, EIP-1559)
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume COINBASE warming applies uniformly to all transaction types since EIP-2929 access lists are universal.

ambiguities.text: The phrase 'at the start of transaction execution' is not precisely defined relative to other initialization steps
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume COINBASE is added to accessed_addresses during the same initialization phase as sender, recipient, and precompiles, before any EVM execution begins.

implicit_assumptions.description: The COINBASE address is known at transaction execution start (block header is available)
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If COINBASE cannot be determined, the warm initialization would fail, breaking transaction execution

implicit_assumptions.description: Contracts that pay block builders directly (MEV protocols) will benefit from this change
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If builders use different addresses for rewards, the gas savings would not materialize

implicit_assumptions.description: EIP-2929 access list gas accounting is correctly implemented across all clients
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Inconsistent warm/cold accounting could cause consensus failures after this change
